models.title: t-statistic for a supplied regression coefficient estimate
models.summary: A regression coefficient t-statistic scales its deviation from a hypothesized value by its supplied standard error.

relationship.locator: Learning Module7, Hypothesis Testing of Linear Regression Coefficients, printed p453 (PDF p463), Equation(16); intercept counterpart p456/PDF466
relationship.translation_notes: The three coefficient-valued ports share one declared coefficient unit Uc, cancelling to a dimensionless statistic. Their generic response-unit strings are placeholders for the uniform context-qualified Uc; for slope binding replace all three units together, never individually. Unlike generic observation standardization, the null port is a coefficient hypothesis and the denominator is its estimation uncertainty.

assumptions: Coefficient estimate, null and standard error refer to the same coefficient, model, units and covariance estimator.
Declared generic coefficient-unit binding isYU forintercept orYU/XU forslope; all three must match.

limitations: A supplied erroneous standard error invalidates inference; CFA Equation18 intercept standard error is separately flagged and must not be used as a verified input.
No p-value or model validity probability is returned.
